uses: A common medicine used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain such as headaches or body aches.
warnings: Do not take more than the label says. Too much paracetamol can seriously damage the liver. Avoid other products that also contain paracetamol.
directions: Follow the product label or a pharmacist's instructions exactly. This page does not give a personal dose.

uses: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine used for pain, fever, and swelling.
warnings: Can irritate the stomach. Avoid if you have certain stomach, kidney, or heart conditions unless a clinician says it is safe.
directions: Take with food if the label says so. Follow the label or a pharmacist's instructions.

uses: An antihistamine used for allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, and itchy eyes.
warnings: May cause drowsiness in some people. Avoid driving or risky activity if you feel sleepy.
directions: Follow the label or a pharmacist's instructions. Do not combine with other sedating medicines without advice.

uses: An antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections.
warnings: Antibiotics do not work on viral illnesses like the common cold. Only use when prescribed. Finish the course as directed.
directions: Use only under a clinician's prescription. Follow their instructions exactly.

uses: A medicine used to help manage blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, alongside diet and activity.
warnings: Only use when prescribed. Tell your clinician about kidney problems or if you become very unwell or dehydrated.
directions: Follow the prescription exactly. Do not change the dose yourself.

uses: A reliever inhaler medicine that opens the airways in asthma.
warnings: Needing your reliever more often than usual can be a sign of worsening asthma. Seek medical advice.
directions: Use exactly as prescribed and as taught by a clinician. This page does not replace an asthma action plan.

uses: A medicine that reduces stomach acid, used for heartburn and certain stomach conditions.
warnings: Long-term use should be discussed with a clinician. It can interact with other medicines.
directions: Follow the label or a clinician's instructions. Swallow capsules whole unless told otherwise.

uses: A mixture of salts and sugar in water used to replace fluids lost through diarrhoea or vomiting.
warnings: Severe dehydration, blood in stool, or persistent vomiting needs medical care. Follow the packet instructions for mixing.
directions: Mix exactly as the packet says with clean water. Do not add extra sugar or salt.
activeIngredients: Sodium chloride, potassium chloride, sodium citrate, glucose
